text.p: Digital Equipment Corp Chief Executive Robert Palmer said the company has a net income goal of seven percent of total revenues by fiscal 1998.

"To achieve our seven percent net income target, we will have to make continued progress in reducing expenses and improving gross margins," Palmer told shareholders at the company's annual meeting in Boston.
For fiscal 1996, Digital reported a net loss of $147 million on revenues of $14.56 billion.

Palmer also said the company is targetting gross margins of 35 percent, research and engineering costs of seven percent of revenues and SG&A costs of 20 percent of revenues for fiscal 1998. He said the company's turnaround is almost complete, but he
still hopes to "significantly" reduce expenses in Europe.

"What I hope to convey is that we have most of the turnaround behind us and that there is good reason to be confident in our ability to achieve competitive levels of growth and profitability and to build our value for shareholders," he said.
Palmer admitted the company may have erred by realigning the sales force and cutting the number of customers handled directly to 1,000 from 10,000.

"My belief is we went a little too far," he said. This summer Digital expanded the direct sales coverage to 2,500 customers, including 1,500 in Europe, which had the unexpected consequence of disrupting the sales force and causing sales to drop off.

However, Palmer said he is optimistic because the U.S. governement business, which was not affected by the changes in the sales force, grew almost 50 percent in the first quarter over the same quarter last year.
